content: Robert Coleman Atkins, MD, was an American physician and cardiologist, born on October 17, 1930, and passing away on April 17, 2003. He is most widely recognized for developing the Atkins Nutritional Approach, commonly referred to as the Atkins Diet. This dietary regimen emphasizes the consumption of low-carbohydrate, high-protein foods, along with leafy vegetables and dietary supplements. Dr. Atkins completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Michigan in 1951 and earned his medical degree from Cornell Medical College in 1955. He subsequently specialized in cardiology and complementary medicine. In the early 2000s, Dr. Atkins developed cardiomyopathy, a condition affecting the heart muscle, which he asserted was unrelated to his dietary practices. On April 18, 2002, he experienced cardiac arrest. Less than a year later, on April 8, 2003, he suffered a severe fall on ice outside his medical office in New York City, resulting in significant head trauma that left him comatose. Despite medical intervention, he succumbed to kidney failure on April 17, 2003. Following his death, controversy arose when the New York City Medical Examiner’s Office mistakenly released his medical records to the Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine, a group advocating for vegetarian diets and associated with PETA. These records indicated that Dr. Atkins weighed approximately 255 pounds (116 kg) at the time of his death, which classified him as obese based on BMI calculations. This information was widely disseminated by media outlets and animal rights organizations, leading to public scrutiny. However, the Atkins company clarified that his weight upon hospital admission was 196 pounds (89 kg) and attributed the apparent weight gain to fluid retention caused by organ failure. Journalist William Leith, who interviewed Dr. Atkins after his cardiac arrest but before his fall, described him as being nearly six feet tall and weighing around 200 pounds, noting that he appeared neither thin nor overweight, with minimal signs of excess weight. On July 31, 2005, Atkins Nutritionals, the company founded by Dr. Atkins in 1989, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in New York. The company faced financial difficulties due to the declining popularity of the Atkins Diet and the emergence of competing high-protein, low-carbohydrate diet plans. By January 10, 2006, the company restructured and emerged from bankruptcy, shifting its focus from promoting the low-carbohydrate diet to marketing prepared nutritional products such as bars and shakes. Dr. Atkins was also a prolific author, publishing numerous books on nutrition, dieting, and health. His works include Dr. Atkins' Diet Revolution (1972), Dr. Atkins' New Diet Revolution (1992, updated in 2002), Dr. Atkins' SuperEnergy Diet (1978), and Dr. Atkins' Vita-Nutrient Solution: Nature's Answers to Drugs (1997), among others. These publications contributed significantly to the widespread popularity of his dietary philosophy and remain influential in discussions of low-carbohydrate nutrition.
